thread:
alex_cs: Hey team, customer reported duplicate completions after an SSE disconnect + reconnect. They saw the same 2 paragraphs generated twice and were billed twice. Repro steps attached.
maya_support: Thanks Alex. Can you paste the repro steps here? Do we have customer id/account? :rotating_light:
alex_cs: Account: acme-analytics. Repro steps from customer: 1) Open SSE stream to /v1/streams/chat 2) Wait ~3s for partial output, then kill connection 3) Reconnect immediately with the same session token 4) Server resumes and re-emits last chunk + continues -> duplicate text and double billing.
raj_runtime: Assigning to me. Quick q: are they using resume tokens (resume_token) or only session id? Also which SDK version?
alex_cs: Customer says they pass X-Session-Token only. No explicit resume_token. SDK: python-sdk v0.9.1.
raj_runtime: That helps. If client reconnects without a resume offset, runtime currently treats it as a fresh consumer in some codepaths and may replay last buffered chunks. Need logs. Can you ask for the stream server logs (trace_id) and the client-side reconnect logs?
maya_support: Sent request for logs and example timeline. Also asked for raw SSE frames if they can capture.
sophia_billing: Billing flagged the two charges. If we confirm duplication due to replay, we can issue a refund and add guardrails to avoid future double-charges. Need repro before reversing.
alex_cs: Customer pasted a short example of frames (sanitized):
```
data: {"seq": 42, "text": "Hello wor"

}
data: {"seq": 43, "text": "ld!\nThis is the rest"}
```
They show seq 42 trailing fragment then reconnection shows seq 42 again.
raj_runtime: Ok that pattern matches a resume race: the server's in-memory prefix buffer had chunk 42, connection dropped after sending first frame but before ack persisted. On reconnect, client didn't provide resume offset so the server re-sent from last stable seq.
raj_runtime: Short-term mitigation: suggest client set a small backoff (200-500ms) and include header `X-Resume-Offset` or `Resume-Token` if SDK supports it. We'll also add server-side dedupe for recent seqs per session id.
maya_support: Customer asked if they must switch SDK right away. They have usage spikes and can't deploy client changes easily.
raj_runtime: Understood. We can push a hotfix to runtime to treat immediate reconnects within 1s as continuation if session id matches, suppress duplicate emissions for seqs that were previously sent but not acked by billing. That reduces duplicates w/o client changes.
sophia_billing: From billing side, do we have a way to identify duplicate billing by seq id? If we suppress server duplicate emission, we should avoid charging twice for same seq tokens.
raj_runtime: We'll mark tokens associated with transient seqs as provisional until end-of-stream confirmation. If we later see a replay of the same seq from same session id within 5s window, we won't double bill. Requires runtime + billing coord.
deploy-bot: New deploy queued: runtime/patch/session-dedupe v1 -> canary in staging.
alex_cs: Great. I've told customer we are investigating and will prioritize a fix. Asked for timeframe.
raj_runtime: ETA: hotfix PR today, deploy to staging tonight, canary to prod tomorrow morning. Will follow up with exact PR link.
maya_support: Customer happy with a workaround but asked for a long-term solution and docs for client-side idempotency keys.
alex_cs: I'll create a support KB draft: recommended headers, sample reconnect backoff (expo capped at 1s), and how to verify SSE resume tokens. Will share for review.
raj_runtime: One more ask for logs: trace_id and backend logs for 2219876543-conn from their timeframe. If they can't provide, we have to run synthetic repro against their prompt.
maya_support: Noted. I'll keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
